Routing evidence:
- Option C (regional office) is valid for south-region claims (both small and large) and at least one large south-region shipment.
- Option C is invalid for all observed east-region requests (small/large invoices and refunds).
- Option C is invalid for observed south-region refunds (large).
- Do not infer size alone determines routing: south claims of both sizes accepted via C.
- For unobserved combinations (e.g., south invoice, east claim/shipment), avoid assuming C; use A/B unless additional policy evidence appears.

Routing evidence:
- A accepted for east small shipment, east small refund, and north small invoice.
- A rejected for south small refund, north small refund, and east large claim.
- B rejected for north small claim and north large refund.
- C accepted for south large shipment; also valid for south claims (small and large) and at least one large south shipment.
- C is invalid for all observed east requests (small/large invoices and refunds), observed south large refund, and prior east claims.
- Do not infer routing from size alone: south claims of both sizes use C.
- Refunds: east small uses A; south small is not A; north small is not A; north large is not B. Correct options for rejected refund cases remain unconfirmed.
- Claims: south uses C; east large is not A or C, so B is the remaining candidate; north small is not B, but its correct option is unconfirmed.
- Shipments: east small uses A; south large uses C.
- Invoices: north small uses A; prior east invoice observations rule out C. 
- Operations memos announce upcoming procedure changes for shipments and claims; do not assume the change is already effective or generalize current routing beyond observed cases.
- For unobserved combinations, avoid guessing; use only confirmed mappings or seek additional policy evidence.

Routing evidence:

- A rejected for south small refund, north small refund (prior case), and east large claim.
- B rejected for north small claim and north large refund.
- C accepted for south shipments (small and large), south claims (small and large), and north small refund (new evidence).
- C is invalid for observed east requests (small/large invoices and refunds) and south large refund; prior east claims also rule out C.
- D accepted for south large invoice, north large claim, and north large and small shipments (new evidence).
- Claims: south uses C; north large uses D; east large is not A or C, making B the remaining candidate. North small is not B, but its correct option remains unconfirmed.
- Refunds: east small uses A; north small now has confirmed C despite an earlier rejection of A; south small and north large are not A/B respectively, with south small still unresolved.
- Shipments: east small uses A; south small/large use C; north large/small use D. Do not generalize D beyond observed cases.
- Invoices: north small uses A; south large uses D. Prior east invoice observations rule out C; other combinations remain unconfirmed.
- Operations memos announce upcoming procedure changes for invoices and shipments; do not assume changes are already effective or universally applicable.
- Avoid guessing for unobserved combinations; use confirmed mappings or seek policy evidence.

Routing evidence:

- Recent rejected: B for east small claim; C for south small refund and south large claim; A for east large shipment; D for north large shipment.
- Earlier accepted mappings remain historical only: C for south small/large claims, C for south shipments, D for north large shipment, and C for north small refund. New conflicting outcomes indicate procedures may depend on timing or request details; do not treat these as universal rules.
- East small refund is repeatedly confirmed as A. East large claim is not A/C, but B was rejected in the latest case, so its current correct option is unresolved.
- North small shipment has recent D acceptance. North large shipment has conflicting D results; current option unresolved.
- South small refund: A was previously ruled out and recent C was rejected; unresolved.
- South large claim: prior C acceptance is contradicted by the latest C rejection; unresolved.
- Invoices: south large D is confirmed by recent evidence; north small A remains historical. East invoice observations rule out C; other combinations remain unconfirmed.
- Claims: north large D is confirmed recently; east small/large and south cases require caution due to conflicting or rejected recent attempts.
- Shipments: recent north small D and east large A rejection; prior south C and north large D results may no longer apply.
- Operations memos announce upcoming claim and shipment procedure changes. Track timing and request details; do not assume changes are already effective or universal.
- Avoid guessing for unobserved or conflicting combinations; use the latest matching evidence or seek explicit policy guidance.

Routing evidence:
- Latest accepted: C for north large refund, east small shipment, south large shipment, and north small refund; D for north small claim; B for east large invoice and south large claim.
- Latest rejected: C for east small claim; D for north small shipment and north large invoice.
- East small refund remains repeatedly confirmed as A.
- East small claim: C rejected; prior B rejection also exists, so unresolved.
- East small shipment: latest C accepted; prior A rejection. Treat C as current evidence, possibly detail/timing-dependent.
- East large invoice: latest B accepted; prior observations rule out C. B is current evidence.
- North small shipment: D accepted previously but rejected most recently; unresolved and likely request-detail/timing-sensitive.
- North large invoice: latest D rejected; historical A only, so unresolved.
- North small refund: latest C accepted, superseding historical uncertainty.
- North large refund: C accepted; new mapping.
- North small claim: latest D accepted.
- South large shipment: latest C accepted, revising earlier uncertainty.
- South large claim: latest B accepted, contradicting prior C results.
- South small refund remains unresolved: A was ruled out and C was rejected.
- North large claim remains recently confirmed as D.
- Earlier accepted mappings are historical only when contradicted; do not generalize across request details.
- Operations memos indicate claim and shipment procedure changes are upcoming or may be taking effect. Track timing, wording, and request details; do not assume universal rules.
- For any conflicting or unobserved combination, use the latest matching evidence cautiously or seek explicit policy guidance.

Routing evidence:
- Current accepted mappings: C for north large refund, north small refund, east small shipment, south large shipment; B for east large invoice; B for south large claim.
- Rejected/latest conflicting mappings: D for north large claim and north small claim; B for south large refund, south large invoice, and previously east? (east large invoice remains B accepted); A for east small claim.
- East small claim is unresolved: A and prior B rejected; C also rejected.
- North small claim is unresolved: D was previously accepted but most recently rejected.
- North large claim is unresolved: D was recently confirmed but is now rejected; do not rely on D.
- North small shipment remains timing/detail-sensitive: D accepted previously, then rejected.
- North large invoice remains unresolved: D rejected; historical A only.
- South large refund is unresolved: latest B rejected; prior evidence insufficient.
- South small refund remains unresolved: A ruled out and C rejected.
- South small invoice is newly unresolved: B rejected; no reliable alternative.
- East large invoice: B accepted repeatedly; prior C ruled out.
- North large refund, north small refund, east small shipment, south large shipment, and south large claim should retain the accepted mappings above, while recognizing detail/timing may matter.
- Shipment procedure change is imminent; revalidate shipment routing around the effective time.
- Claim procedure changes may also affect results. Track timing, wording, size, request type, and region; never generalize from one detail combination.
- For conflicts or unseen combinations, use the latest matching evidence cautiously or seek explicit policy guidance.
